title: Extraction Result — the shape ocr.js returns, v1
description:
The return contract of email-ingestor-lib's ocrImagePdf()/ocrImage(). Until now this shape was implicit, unversioned and unvalidated, which is exactly how PR #35 (2026-08-15) could add ocrPartial/ocrPagesExtracted/ocrPagesTotal to the PDF path and have two of the three consumers silently drop all three with nothing failing. Unlike intake-contract.v1 — which is hand-copied into four repos and has already drifted — this file SHIPS INSIDE the package every consumer already depends on, so there is exactly one copy. Import it as email-ingestor-lib/contracts/extraction-result.v1.schema.json.

Discriminated on `ok`. MIGRATION HAZARD: today a failed extraction returns bare `null`, and callers test truthiness (`if (!result) ...`). A failure object is TRUTHY, so any caller reached before it is updated would read a failure as a success. Consumers must be taught to check `.ok` BEFORE ocr.js starts returning failure objects — same consumer-first ordering the envelope contract requires.

rawText.description: Extracted text. May be empty when tier-2/tier-3 salvage recovered nothing.

structured.description: Receipt-shaped subset {vendor, amount, currency, date, line_items}. Null unless parsed.is_receipt was true.

parsed.description: Full JSON object from UNIVERSAL_PROMPT, snake_case. Null when the response could not be parsed as JSON — note tiers 2 and 3 of the salvage path return text with parsed:null, so a truncated dense document loses every structured field while still looking successful.

ocrPartial.description: TRUE when this extraction does not represent the whole document, for ANY reason — an oversized PDF was page-split, or the model hit max_tokens. Always present. Today it is conditionally spread onto the PDF path only and is absent entirely from ocrImage(), so a caller cannot distinguish 'complete' from 'field not emitted on this path' (F7).

ocrPagesExtracted.description: Pages actually sent to the model. Null when no split occurred or the page count is unknown.

ocrPagesTotal.description: Pages in the source document. Null when pdfinfo could not determine it — best-effort by design, so null here does NOT imply a complete read.

ocrTruncated.description: TRUE when the model stopped on max_tokens. ocr.js already computes this (stop_reason === 'max_tokens') and today throws it away into a log-message suffix, making a truncated extraction indistinguishable from a clean one to every caller (F6).

failureReason.description: Why nothing was extracted. Today all five collapse to a bare `null` with no code (F5) — which is the root cause of the 2026-08-16 finding that four format classes had failed silently and accumulated 766 unusable documents. An unprocessable file must be able to say WHY.

detail.description: Optional human-readable detail. Never include file contents or a full path — this value reaches logs and telemetry.
